He grew up in [[Milton, Ontario]], and attended [[Athlete Institute|Orangeville Prep]] in [[Orangeville, Ontario]], where he played [[association football|soccer]] and [[volleyball]] before picking up [[basketball]] in grade 11. He became roommates with [[Denver Nuggets]] guard [[Jamal Murray]]. Alexander played [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] basketball with the CIA Bounce, teaming up with Murray.{{cite web|title=Kyle Alexander – Men's Basketball – University of Tennessee Athletics|url=https://utsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6743|website=UTSports.com|accessdate=October 4, 2019}} ==College career== Alexander played college basketball for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]] for four years.{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=August 6, 2019 |title=Kyle Alexander on sticking with Miami Heat: 'My best basketball is ahead of me' |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2019/08/06/kyle-alexander-miami-heat-tennessee-vols-basketball/1880180001/ |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=[[Knoxville News Sentinel]]}} As a senior, he averaged 7.3 points, 6.6 rebounds, 1.7 blocks and 23.8 minutes per game. He helped lead the team to the Sweet Sixteen, shooting 61.4 percent from the field and 42.9 percent from three-point range. ==Professional career== ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2019–2020)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Alexander joined the [[Miami Heat]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite news |last=Lay |first=Ken |date=July 5, 2019 |title=Kyle Alexander grabs four rebounds in Heat's rout of China |url=https://volswire.usatoday.com/2019/07/05/kyle-alexander-grabs-four-rebounds-in-heats-rout-of-china/ |access-date=October 2, 2019 |work=Vols Wire|publisher=USA Today}} On July 15, 2019, he was signed by the Heat to a training camp contract.{{cite news|title=HEAT Signs Kyle Alexander|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-kyle-alexander-190715|accessdate=October 2, 2019|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=July 15, 2019}}{{cite news|last1=Winderman|first1=Ira|title=Heat sign summer prospect Kyle Alexander to camp contract|url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-kyle-alexander-20190715-lvb3xy3mcrajraeturbi2fnkou-story.html|accessdate=October 2, 2019|work=Sun Sentinel|date=July 16, 2019}} Following training camp, Alexander was added to the roster of the Heat's [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite news |title= Skyforce Announces 2019–20 Training Camp Roster |url= https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-2019-20-training-camp-roster/ |accessdate= November 2, 2019 |publisher= [[National Basketball Association]] |date= October 27, 2019 |archive-date= November 2, 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20191102180042/https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-announces-2019-20-training-camp-roster/ |url-status= dead }} ===Miami Heat (2020)=== On January 15, 2020, Alexander signed a two-way contract with the [[Miami Heat]].{{cite news|title=Kyle Alexander gets Two-Way opportunity With HEAT|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-signs-kyle-alexander-to-two-way-contract-200115|accessdate=January 15, 2020|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |date=January 15, 2020}} The following day, it was announced that he was sidelined with a knee injury.{{cite news |title=Heat's Kyle Alexander: Sidelined with knee injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/heats-kyle-alexander-sidelined-with-knee-injury/ |accessdate=February 6, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 16, 2020}} He made his NBA debut on August 6, 2020, where he played one minute off the bench and recorded one rebound in a 130–116 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite news |last1=Winderman |first1=Ira |title=Miami Heat prospects wind up with a most unusual NBA summer school |url=https://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/miami-heat/fl-sp-miami-heat-notebook-wednesday-20200812-sbbf5mcamjcexpgx7revtft5ue-story.html |accessdate=August 12, 2020 |work=[[Sun-Sentinel]] |date=August 12, 2020}} The Heat reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]], but lost in 6 games to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. ===Fuenlabrada (2020–2022)=== On December 2, 2020, Alexander signed with [[Baloncesto Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{cite web |last1=Yahyabeyoglu |first1=Fersu |title=Kyle Alexander joins Fuenlabrada |url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Spain/news/656335/Kyle-Alexander-joins-Fuenlabrada |website=Eurobasket |access-date=December 2, 2020 |date=December 2, 2020}} He averaged 9 points and 6.2 rebounds per game. On August 23, 2021, he re-signed with the team.{{cite web |title=Urbas Fuenlabrada re-signs Kyle Alexander |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/urbas-fuenlabrada-re-signs-kyle-alexander/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 23, 2021 |date=August 23, 2021}} ===Scarborough Shooting Stars (2022)=== On May 16, 2022, Alexander signed with the [[Scarborough Shooting Stars]] of the [[CEBL]]. ===Valencia (2022–2023)=== On July 22, 2022, Alexander signed with [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/valencia-basket-signs-kyle-alexander/|title=Valencia Basket signs Kyle Alexander|date=July 22, 2022|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 8, 2022}} On June 26, 2023, he parted ways with the club.{{cite web|title= Kyle Alexander terminates his contract with Valencia Basket|url=https://valenciabasket.com/?p=noticias¬icia=9917&lang=en|publisher=[[Valencia Basket]]|date=June 26, 2023|access-date=June 28, 2023}} ===Hapoel Tel Aviv (2023–2024)=== On July 26, 2023, he signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/kyle-alexander-joins-hapoel-shlomo-tel-aviv-for-the-upcoming-season/|title=Kyle Alexander Joins Hapoel Shlomo Tel Aviv for the Upcoming Season|date=July 26, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 29, 2023}} ===Türk Telekom (2024–2026)=== On July 11, 2024, Alexander signed with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=TT_Basketbol |number=1811320621747351889 |title=Kyle Alexander Türk Telekom’da }} During the [[2024–25 EuroCup Basketball|2024–25 EuroCup]] season, Alexander established himself as one of the competition's leading defensive centers. He led the EuroCup in blocked shots, averaging 2.2 blocks per game, while also recording 6.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/players/kyle-alexander/profile/011973/ |title=Kyle Alexander |website=EuroCup |publisher=Euroleague Basketball |access-date=9 August 2026 }} On September 10, 2025, Alexander renewed his contract with Türk Telekom for the 2025–26 season.{{Cite tweet |user=TT_Basketbol |number=1965821790510526841 |title=Kyle Alexander yeniden Türk Telekom’da }} He completed the 2025–26 campaign averaging 9.7 points, 5.7 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.1 blocks across 49 appearances in all competitions.{{cite web |url=https://www.paokbc.gr/en/news/team/3584-kyle-alexander-joins-paok-through-2028 |title=Kyle Alexander joins PAOK through 2028 |website=PAOK BC |date=19 June 2026 |access-date=9 August 2026 }} ===PAOK Thessaloniki (2026–present)=== On June 19, 2026, Alexander signed a two-year contract with [[PAOK BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]], keeping him with the club through the end of the 2027–28 season. He joined PAOK as part of the club's roster reconstruction under head coach [[Andrea Trinchieri]], with the club highlighting his athleticism, defensive presence and efficiency as key elements of his game. Following his signing, Alexander stated that the opportunity to work with Trinchieri was an important factor in his decision to join PAOK, noting that the two had previously come close to working together.{{cite web |url=https://www.paokbc.gr/el/nea/sunenteuxeis/3585-kyle-alexander-coach-trinchieri |title=Kyle Alexander: «Είμαι ενθουσιασμένος που θα παίξω στον ΠΑΟΚ και θα συνεργαστώ με τον || .638 || 4.9 || .3 || .3 || 1.4 || 4.6 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Alexander is the son of Joseph and Audrey Alexander. His father Joseph played college basketball for the [[Niagara Purple Eagles men's basketball|Niagara Purple Eagles]] from 1982 to 1986. He has two sisters, named [[Kayla Alexander|Kayla]] and Kesia. His sister Kayla is also a professional basketball player and was a member of the [[Canada women's national basketball team]] for [[Canada at the Olympics|Team Canada]] at the [[2020 Olympics]] in [[Tokyo]],{{cite web |title=Kayla ALEXANDER |url=https://olympics.com/en/athletes/kayla-alexander |website=Olympics.com |publisher=International Olympic Committee |access-date=November 5, 2022}} and formerly of the [[Minnesota Lynx]] of the [[Women's National Basketball Association|WNBA]]. ==References== {{reflist}} ==External links== {{commons}} *{{basketballstats}} *[https://utsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6743 Tennessee Volunteers bio] {{PAOK B.C. current roster}} {{Canada Squad 2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Alexander, Kyle}} [[Category:1996 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup players]] [[Category:21st-century Canadian sportsmen]] [[Category:Baloncesto Fuenlabrada players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Toronto]] [[Category:Black Canadian basketball players]] [[Category:Black Canadian sportsmen]] [[Category:Canada men's national basketball team players]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in Spain]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in Turkey]] [[Category:Canadian expatriate basketball people in the United States]] [[Category:Canadian men's basketball players]] [[Category:Centers (basketball)]] [[Category:Liga ACB players]] [[Category:Miami Heat players]] [[Category:NBA players from Canada]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Scarborough Shooting Stars players]] [[Category:Sioux Falls Skyforce players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Milton, Ontario]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Scarborough, Ontario]] [[Category:Tennessee Volunteers basketball players]] [[Category:Türk Telekom B.K. players]] [[Category:Undrafted NBA players]] [[Category:Valencia Basket players]]
